{{nihongo|'''Ōgamiyama Jinja'''|大神山神社 |Ōgamiyama Jinja}} is a [[Shinto]] [[Shrines|shrine]], in [[Daisen, Tottori|Daisen]], [[Tottori Prefecture|Tottori]], [[Japan]]. A number of its structures have been designated [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Properties]].

==Origins==
Ōgamiyama Jinja is a complex of Shinto shrines, which were created to worship [[Daisen (mountain)|Daisen]]. Daisen has been worshiped as a holy mountain at least since the 8th century. Originally this shrine was constructed as a simple building {{convert|998|m|ft}} above sea level on a peak {{convert|1725|m|ft}} in height. The small building was set up as a shrine in the [[Heian period]].

==History==
The original location of this shrine is covered by heavy snow in winter, so another branch of this shrine was built at the foot of the mountain. It is called the ''winter shrine''. In turn, the original shrine was called the ''summer shrine''. 
The winter shrine was originally built at Maruyama, [[Kishimoto, Tottori|Kishimoto]], but moved to Fukumahara and Odaka in [[Yonago, Tottori|Yonago]]. The summer shrine has remained in its original location since Heian Period.
With the [[Shinbutsu bunri]], literally Shinto-Buddhism-separation after the Meiji restoration, this shrine was formally separated from [[Daisen-ji]], and the summer shrine was renamed ''Okumiya'' of Ogami Jinja and the Buddhist objects of worship were removed.
The current main object of worship is "Oanamuchi no Kami".

In the [[modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]], Ōgamiyama was listed among the 3rd class of nationally significant shrines or {{nihongo|''[[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei-shōsha]]''|国幣小社}}.

==Important Cultural Properties==
* Okumiya [[Honden]] - [[heiden (Shinto)|Heiden]] - [[haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1805)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2949 |title=Database of Registered National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=28 April 2011}}</ref>
* [[Setsumatsusha|Massha]] Shimoyama [[Honden]] - [[heiden (Shinto)|Heiden]] - [[haiden (Shinto)|Haiden]] (1805)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2950 |title=Database of Registered National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=28 April 2011}}</ref>
* Large stone [[Torii]] (1854)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/101/00002812 |title=Database of Registered National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=28 April 2011}}</ref>
